subject.title: [Bug] Sandbox validateEnvVarValue base64 heuristic false-positives on legitimate long alphanumeric values

question: Should OpenClaw narrow the sandbox credential-data warning to structured base64 values only when the env var name is credential-like, accepting fewer warnings for neutral or nonstandard names?
rationale: The false positive is source-reproducible, but reducing advisory sandbox credential-warning coverage is a security-boundary policy choice that automation should not make alone.

options.title: Approve narrow warning policy
options.body: Refresh the linked PR onto current main and land the key-aware structured-base64 sanitizer if sandbox/security owners accept the reduced neutral-name warning coverage.

options.title: Preserve broader warning coverage
options.body: Keep the issue open and ask for a different heuristic that reduces false positives without requiring credential-like names.

options.title: Close as intentional policy
options.body: If broad value warnings are the desired sandbox posture, close this as not planned and document that the warning is intentionally conservative.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow warning policy
recommendation.body: Refresh the linked PR onto current main and land the key-aware structured-base64 sanitizer if sandbox/security owners accept the reduced neutral-name warning coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete introduced the sanitizer and adjacent tests, making them the strongest history-backed owner for this warning-policy choice.
